newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CSOB, CIBC WOOD SIGNS CZK 500 MLN CREDIT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CSOB, CIBC WOOD SIGNS CZK 500 MLN CREDIT.

text.p: Czech bank Ceskoslovenksa Obchodni Banka (CSOB) said on Friday it had signed a 500 million crown, 12.5 year credit facility with Candian bank CIBC Wood Gundy.
A CSOB statement said CIBC Wood Gundy would use the funds to help it in financing the construction of an electrical generating station that the Canadian bank is participating in.
Further details of the credit were not immediately available.
ECK Generating sro, a Czech-U.S. joint venture, is building the new $400 million, 350 megawatt power plant in Kladno, some 25km (15 miles) northwest of Prague.

ECK Generating, is partly owned by Independent Power CZ, a unit of California- based ACT Inc, with involvement also of NRG Energy, a subsidiary of U.S. power utility Northern States Power Co , and Nations' Energy Corp. a subsidiary of Tucson Electric Power Co.

Financing for the project is also to be financed by 15-year credits from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Japan's Nissho Iwai Corporation, as well as from CSOB and the Czech savings bank Ceska Sporitelna a.s..
The IFC is granting $85 million in credits, Nissho Iwai $65 million, with CSOB and Sporitelna combining to provide $115 million in credit.
Swiss-Swedish engineering concern ABB, one of the main contractors of the plnat's construction, also will provide a credit of $37.5 million.
ECK has already signed a 20-year contract to supply power to the distribution company Stredoceska Energeticka a.s. from the plant, which is to be completed in 1999.
The ECK plant will also provide communal heating, from the combined coal/gas plant, to the city of Kladno.
